run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: During the authorized window only one workload in astronomy-shop was changed: Deployment frontend-proxy reached revision 2 (generation 2) while all 22 other deployments stayed at revision 1. Its replica set frontend-proxy-88764bfbb was created at 2026-11-21T10:48:27Z with the Envoy entrypoint replaced by a single-process Perl 'edge request filter' (`/usr/bin/perl -e ...`) and with fault-style settings switched on: WAF_RULE_ENABLED="true" and WAF_RULE_REGEX="^([a-zA-Z]+)*$"; the image digest is unchanged (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-frontend-proxy), so this is a configuration-only replacement. The old Envoy pod frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5-4mjr9 logged ENVOY_SIGTERM at 10:48:30.355Z and exited at 10:48:30.372Z, so the entire shop's edge traffic moved to the new proxy ~15 s before the observation window closed. The script evaluates the regex against a `waf` query parameter and, when that parameter is non-empty, answers 200 'ok' without proxying to the frontend; the pattern itself is a classic catastrophic-backtracking (ReDoS) form in a single-threaded accept loop, so the leading hypothesis is that frontend-proxy is the faulty component and will hang or short-circuit user traffic. I could not observe the filter executing, nor any resulting error or latency, inside the window, so the conclusion is partial. Separately, errors at 10:48:02–10:48:13 (frontend 500s from ECONNREFUSED to cart:8080 and flagd:8013, recommendation ECONNREFUSED product-catalog:8080, ad 501 ms flagd ResolveBoolean deadlines) are startup transients: every dependency's blackbox probe returned to 1 by 10:48:10, ad GetAds was back to 4 ms by 10:48:24 and cart handled cart traffic normally. The only unexplained residue is the blackbox probe cart.astronomy-shop:8080, which stayed at 0 for every 15 s sample through 10:48:45 while cart itself was healthy.

claims.text: Only Deployment frontend-proxy was changed during the window: it is at metadata.generation 2 with deployment.kubernetes.io/revision "2", while all other 22 deployments in astronomy-shop (accounting, ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, flagd, fraud-detection, frontend, grafana, image-provider, jaeger, kafka, llm, payment, postgresql, product-catalog, product-reviews, quote, recommendation, shipping, valkey-cart) are at generation 1 / revision "1".

frontend-proxy has two ReplicaSets: frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5 (created 2026-11-21T10:46:55Z, revision 1) whose command was the stock Envoy entrypoint `/bin/sh -c "envsubst < envoy.tmpl.yaml | sed ... > envoy.yaml && exec envoy -c envoy.yaml"` and which now has 0 replicas, and frontend-proxy-88764bfbb (created 2026-11-21T10:48:27Z, revision 2) whose command is ["/usr/bin/perl","-e"] with env WAF_RULE_REGEX="^([a-zA-Z]+)*$" and WAF_RULE_ENABLED="true" and which has 1 ready replica.

The frontend-proxy Deployment's current container spec replaces Envoy with a Perl script named 'edge request filter' that binds ENVOY_PORT (8080), reads the request, extracts a `waf` query parameter, applies the rule when WAF_RULE_ENABLED is not "false" (WAF_RULE_ENABLED="true", WAF_RULE_REGEX="^([a-zA-Z]+)*$"), logs a request_filter_eval line with elapsedSeconds, then returns `HTTP/1.1 200 OK ... ok` and closes without contacting the upstream whenever the candidate is non-empty; otherwise it forwards to FRONTEND_HOST:FRONTEND_PORT (frontend:8080). The image is unchanged (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-frontend-proxy) and limits are cpu 100m / memory 65Mi.

The cutover of the edge proxy happened at the end of the window: the Envoy pod frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5-4mjr9 logged "caught ENVOY_SIGTERM" at 2026-11-21T10:48:30.355Z and "exiting" at 2026-11-21T10:48:30.372Z, while the new pod frontend-proxy-88764bfbb-2gxkq started at 2026-11-21T10:48:27Z, is Running, ready=true and has 0 restarts.

Between 10:48:02 and 10:48:13 the shop had dependency connect failures: recommendation got Connection refused to product-catalog (10.96.179.177:8080) on ListProducts, frontend got ECONNREFUSED to cart (10.96.47.215:8080) on CartService/GetCart and CartService/AddItem (gRPC status 14) and returned HTTP 500, and checkout failed with 'failed to charge card ... connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.51.84:8013' (flagd); ad's flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean spans failed with rpc.grpc.status_code=4 after ~501 ms and cart's flagd EventStream/POST failed with 'Connection refused (flagd:8013)'. These propagated as 500s through frontend-proxy and load-generator.

All blackbox HTTP probes except cart recovered: every 15 s sample shows ad, checkout, currency, email, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, kafka, payment, product-catalog, product-reviews, quote, recommendation and shipping at probe_success=1 from 10:48:10 onward, while cart.astronomy-shop:8080 remained probe_success=0 in every sample from 10:46:00 until the last sample at 10:48:45.

ad recovered by 10:48:24-10:48:30: three oteldemo.AdService/GetAds spans took 4056-4447 us with rpc.grpc.status_code=0, resolve/getAdsByCategory work took 61-89 us, and flagd's ResolveBoolean server spans answered in 9-156 us with rpc.grpc.status_code=0.

cart itself was healthy through the end of the window: its log shows 'Now listening on: http://[::]:8080' at 10:48:06.743Z, 'Application started' at 10:48:06.748Z, successful Valkey connection, and continuous AddItemAsync/GetCartAsync/EmptyCartAsync calls from 10:48:09 through 10:48:27.338Z; its pod has no readinessProbe configured (probes: [null]).

No failure of frontend-proxy itself is observed inside the window: probe_success for frontend-proxy.astronomy-shop:8080 was 1 at the last two samples (10:48:30 and 10:48:45), the new Perl pod is ready with 0 restarts, and the newest frontend-proxy error spans returned by Jaeger are the proxied 500s at 10:48:05-10:48:09, i.e. from the Envoy pod before the cutover.

Root cause hypothesis: Deployment frontend-proxy (revision 2) is the faulty component. Its `edge request filter` is a single-threaded Perl accept loop, and WAF_RULE_REGEX="^([a-zA-Z]+)*$" is a catastrophic-backtracking pattern; a `waf` value consisting of a long alphanumeric run followed by a non-letter would make the regex engine backtrack exponentially, block the only accept loop and stall every request through the edge proxy, while a plain non-empty `waf` value would short-circuit the request to a bare 200 'ok' instead of the proxied page.

Rejected as the root cause: the 10:48:02-10:48:13 cascade of ECONNREFUSED/DEADLINE_EXCEEDED errors against flagd:8013, cart:8080 and product-catalog:8080. Those dependencies were still starting at that moment and recovered inside the same window - every probe_success returned to 1 by 10:48:10, ad GetAds was 4 ms at 10:48:24, cart served cart calls continuously and all those services run the unmodified revision-1 templates.

Alternative candidate kept open: flagd unavailability/latency at 10:48:02-10:48:10 (ResolveBoolean DEADLINE_EXCEEDED after ~501 ms in ad and recommendation, ECONNREFUSED flagd:8013 in cart and payment) is a real dependency-level fault signature observed on several callers, but flagd's own probes returned to 1 at 10:48:10 and its resolveBoolean server spans answered in 9-156 us by 10:48:24, so the evidence supports a startup transient rather than a continuing fault.

Compare the frontend-proxy Deployment against its revision-1 template and roll it back to the Envoy entrypoint (or set WAF_RULE_ENABLED="false" and replace WAF_RULE_REGEX="^([a-zA-Z]+)*$" with a non-backtracking, time-bounded check), then confirm whether the load generator sends a `waf` query parameter and read the new pod's 'request_filter_eval' elapsedSeconds lines to verify whether the filter actually blocked traffic.

Check the blackbox probe module and target for cart.astronomy-shop:8080 before treating the persistent probe_success=0 as an application fault: cart's own logs show it listening on 8080 and serving gRPC cart calls, its pod has no readinessProbe, and no cart error spans were produced after 10:48:10.

gaps: No observation exists after the authorized window end 2026-11-21T10:48:45Z, so the effect of the frontend-proxy cutover (which completed at 10:48:30.372Z) on latency, errors or probe success is unknown.

The declared WAF filtering was not seen executing: the Loki query {namespace="astronomy-shop"} |= "request_filter_eval" over 10:20:00-10:48:45Z returned no lines, and fetch_pod_logs for frontend-proxy-88764bfbb-2gxkq returned 0 lines (only an OpenSearch 'waf_logtype.json' line matched the string 'waf' in that window).
It is unknown whether the load generator (or any client) sends a `waf` query parameter, so whether a request ever reached the injected filter cannot be established from the available logs.

When and by whom the frontend-proxy Deployment template was changed (generation 1 -> 2 at 2026-11-21T10:48:27Z) is unknown; no change-history integration is available in this Run and no Kubernetes event naming the change was found.

The persistent probe_success=0 for cart.astronomy-shop:8080 through 10:48:45 is unexplained: cart's application logs show normal operation and its pod is ready, but the blackbox probe module/target configuration was not inspected.

Prometheus history is very short: application span metrics (traces_span_metrics_*) have samples only from about 10:48:00 and blackbox/kube series from about 10:45:15, so no pre-incident baseline exists and rate()/increase() over 2m returned no data; no latency trend can be claimed.

Not checked: the 'observe' namespace (Prometheus/Loki stack) and any non-Kubernetes change channel; the otel-collector-agent DaemonSet pods were replaced at 10:48:15-10:48:20Z (SuccessfulDelete/SuccessfulCreate events) and its telemetry-export failures were not investigated as a candidate cause.
